title: The cord of the heirs laid twice round the gathering-house floor
summary: On Oidhche an Dòrlaich the keepers bring the cord of the heirs down from its chest and lay it from the hearth to the door and back, with lamps set along its length. Nine plain, unmarked knives are laid out for the nine lines that will cut it.

title: Murchadh Mòr cuts the cord first
summary: Murchadh Mòr, eldest living son of the king and near two thousand nine hundred years old, cuts the cord in one stroke exactly where he had long meant to, and takes up the great share of the north, from Baile Mòr mhòr to the high passes.

title: Eithne nic Ailein's knife cuts through a knot
summary: Eithne nic Ailein, youngest of the nine eldest lines, kneels long over her place on the cord and cuts through a knot rather than between two, leaving one heir's line divided between her share and the next.

title: Ciorstaidh cut through and claimed by two shares
summary: Ciorstaidh of the salt shore, whose knot is cut through by Eithne's knife, answers the two lords quarrelling over her with "I'll take both." It is let stand: the first of the double oaths sworn that night.

title: Eleven knots cut through in one night
summary: Where the nine knives cross the cord's thickest stretches, eleven knots in all are cut through rather than between. Eleven households find themselves sworn to two lords at once; most pay both oaths rather than contest them.

title: The western share sworn to Fionnghal nic Ailein
summary: Fionnghal nic Ailein cuts her length of the cord clean and takes the western share, with its seat on the harbour at Ros dhomhain.

title: The salt shore sworn to Artair mac Ailein
summary: Artair mac Ailein, who had argued least of the nine that summer, takes the share of the salt shore, seated at the western Baile ghorm.

title: The eastern share sworn to Cormac mac Ailein
summary: Cormac mac Ailein takes the eastern share, seated at Caol shean, in which the silver of Muileann chiar will one day be found.

title: The four lesser shares sworn to Ùna, Coll, Gormlaith and Tadhg
summary: The last four of the nine cut their lengths in quick succession: Ùna nic Ailein takes the north-west at Muileann àrsaidh, Coll mac Ailein the hills of the Abhainn fhionn at Ceann àrsaidh, Gormlaith nic Ailein the south-east at Tobar dhearg, and Tadhg mac Ailein the Abhainn ìseal and the Hawk bay at Cnoc bheag.

title: The cord of the heirs lies in nine pieces
summary: With the ninth cut made, the cord no longer runs the floor of the gathering-house whole. It lies in nine lengths, one over each lord's arm, with the loose ends of the eleven double knots hanging free between them.

title: The Red Hill declares itself sworn to nobody
summary: The holder of the Red Hill, whose line had sworn to Ailean Mòr alone and to no lord of a share, stands up on the night of the handful and says his oath died with the king, and that the Red Hill is that night sworn to nobody at all.

title: Three great shares claim the Red Hill
summary: Murchadh Mòr and two other lords of the nine cross the floor at once to claim the ownerless Red Hill. None yields, and none of the three can make the claim stand that night or for long after.

title: The Hall's ground confirmed in no share
summary: Aodh Crom reminds the nine, on the night of the handful, that the hill of the slab and the gathering-house and the valley about it, as walked by the keepers, lie in no share, as sworn at the Binding, and are not to be argued afresh.

title: The lengths of cord carried out of the gathering-house
summary: At dawn the nine lords go out through the door of the gathering-house one after another, each with his length of the cord folded or coiled over his arm, and their households follow, so that the valley empties along nine roads at once.
